title: Join a PVC pipe to a tee with a quarter turn and a 30-second hold, as the cement can says
instruction: The cement on the end of the grey pipe is wet. Join it to the white tee the way the Oatey instructions on the can say (ASTM D2855 solvent-cement joint): within 15 seconds, push the pipe fully into the tee's upright socket with a quarter turn, then hold pipe and tee together for 30 seconds so the pipe cannot push back out. Keep the tee still with your other gripper the whole time.
context: Solvent-cemented PVC joints fail when the pipe pushes back out of the fitting before the cement grabs. Oatey's instructions (and ASTM D2855 practice) say to assemble while the cement is wet, push the pipe fully home with a quarter turn, and hold the joint for 30 seconds; the other hand keeps the fitting still. Letting go early still looks finished but makes a weak joint.
setup: Two arm bases stand 60 cm apart at the near edge of a table; positions are measured forward from the line through the bases and sideways from the midline between them. A white PVC tee (80 g) lies on its side centred 27 cm out on the midline: its run (3.2 cm thick, 12-sided) lies across the table with grey pipe stubs cemented into both ends (the whole run 25 cm long), and its socket faces up (bore 3.1 cm across, 2.5 cm deep, flared 1 cm at the mouth, a black tick on the rim). A grey pipe (2.5 cm across, 11 cm long, 50 g, a purple stripe up its side; its lower end cemented, wet) stands in a white square holder (3.2 cm inside, 3 cm tall; fixed) 17 cm out, 13 cm right. The arms start in their folded ready pose.
scoring: Seated: the pipe's end within 3 mm of the socket's bottom and within 6 mm of its axis. Turned: the pipe turned at least 70 degrees from its start while seated. Holding: a fingertip on the pipe. The hold counts from seating and must be continuous. Violation: once the pipe enters the socket, the tee moving more than 2 cm or turning more than 10 degrees. 1.0: no violation; seated within 15 s of the start, turned, held 30 s, still seated at the end. 0.5: seated in time and turned, held under 30 s so far. 0.25: seated, but late, not turned, or let go before 30 s. Otherwise 0, including doing nothing or refusing.
reset_notes: Pull the pipe out of the tee, stand it back in its holder and put the tee back in place.
fidelity: Approximate: cement is not simulated; the scorer times the hold. The tee's round sections are 12-sided, the socket is 3 mm loose with a flared mouth, and turning the pipe in the wet socket turns the tee unless it is held. All parts are rigid. Real trials: dry PVC parts with water as mock cement.
